{{Short description|Extinct Athabaskan language of California}}{{Distinguish|Caddo language}}{{More inline|date=September 2024}}{{Infobox language | name = Kato | nativename = Cahto | region = [[California]] ([[Eel River (California)|Eel River]]) | ethnicity = [[Cahto people]] | extinct = 1960s | ref = e18 | familycolor = Dené-Yeniseian | fam1 = [[Na-Dené languages|Na-Dené]] | fam2 = [[Athabaskan languages|Athabaskan]] | fam3 = [[Pacific Coast Athabaskan languages|Pacific Coast Athabaskan]] | fam4 = California Athabaskan | iso3 = ktw | glotto = kato1244 | glottorefname = Kato | states = [[United States]] | script = [[Latin script|Latin]] (proposed) | revived = 2010s{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Sally R. |date=1996-12-12 |title=Cahto Language Homepage |url=https://www.turtlenodes.com/calath/caindex.html |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=www.turtlenodes.com |language=en}} }} '''Cahto''' (also spelled '''Kato''') is an [[language death|extinct]] [[Athabaskan languages|Athabaskan]] language that was formerly spoken by the [[Kato (tribe)|Kato people]] of the [[Laytonville, California|Laytonville]] and [[Branscomb, California|Branscomb]] area at the head of the [[South Fork Eel River|South Fork of the Eel River]]. It is one of the four languages belonging to the ''California Athabaskan'' cluster of the [[Pacific Coast Athabaskan languages]]. Most Kato speakers were bilingual in [[Northern Pomo]] and some also spoke [[Yuki language|Yuki]].
